haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, the reservation becomes EXPIRED by Inventory's timer and stock goes back on sale. A claim can still succeed if every line is still free.
haiku-low.q2: Before the charge. Inventory checks all lines and reserves nothing if any is short. Order sets REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer sees the short items, and no payment is requested.
haiku-low.q3: The charge uses the order id as the idempotency key, and retries reuse that key. Payment creates a payment only if none exists for the order id, so the customer is charged once.
haiku-low.q4: If any line was sold elsewhere, the claim is refused. Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and emails the customer. Payment automatically refunds the full amount. The cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q5: Only on OrderConfirmed, when Cart empties it. If checkout fails, the cart stays unchanged and the customer can retry.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service coordinates each step and records the overall outcome. Its Orders table holds each checkout's status, such as PENDING, RESERVED or PAID.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook with the event id and order id to Payment. Payment publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker, which Order consumes. Payment may also poll status at 35 minutes.
haiku-low.q8: Payment inserts each provider event id into processed_events, which has a unique constraint. A repeat returns 200 and does nothing. Order also acts only when the order is in the expected status.
haiku-low.q9: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined, and Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED and asks Inventory to release the hold once. If the release fails, the expiry timer frees the stock.
haiku-low.q10: Order checks its status. If RESERVED, it asks Inventory to claim. If already FAILED or PAYMENT_FAILED, it does not claim and requests a refund. Inventory refuses a claim if any line is sold elsewhere.
haiku-low.q11: The refund is retried with backoff using the same key and marked REFUND_RETRYING. After N failures it becomes REFUND_NEEDS_ATTENTION, ops are alerted, and retries continue. It is tracked as a refund row in Payment.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published by Order after the claim succeeds, causes the Cart service to empty the cart.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes. If not claimed, a timer (every minute) marks the HELD reservation EXPIRED and stock goes back on sale. A later claim can still re-take the lines if stock is free.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charge. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, the short items are returned, order is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, no payment is requested.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) sent with every charge retry, so the provider charges only once.
sonnet.q4: Claim is refused, order set CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, customer emailed, full automatic refund via RefundRequested; later REFUNDED once the provider confirms.
sonnet.q5: Emptied only when the order is CONFIRMED (on OrderConfirmed event). On any failure the cart stays unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Order service (the coordinator) starts each step; the record is the order's status stored in Order's own database.
sonnet.q7: Provider sends a webhook to Payment's endpoint; Payment sets PAID/DECLINED and publishes a PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined event on the broker, which Order consumes. (Also a 35-minute status-check timer fallback.)
sonnet.q8: Payment inserts the provider event id into processed_events (unique); if already there it returns 200 and does nothing. Downstream, services act on an event only if their record is in the expected status (Order only while RESERVED), and Payment creates a payment/refund only if none exists for that order id.
sonnet.q9: Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED on the PaymentDeclined event and asks Inventory to release the hold (one try). If that fails, the 1-minute expiry timer frees the stock anyway.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim, which decides in one local transaction: hold intact means mark SOLD; hold lapsed but stock still free means re-take all lines and fulfil; any line sold elsewhere means refuse, so cancel and refund.
sonnet.q11: Refund row status becomes REFUND_RETRYING and Payment retries with backoff using the same key; after N failures REFUND_NEEDS_ATTENTION, ops alerted, keeps retrying. Tracked as a stored refund row in Payment's database.
sonnet.q12: Order sets CONFIRMED and publishes OrderConfirmed; the Cart service empties the cart on that event.
